name: Spellsinger
body:
In the Realms of Magic, spellsingers are more than just sorcerers who sing or bards with more powerful spells. They are their own unique group of spellcasters, capable of weaving music into magic. Once members of a great set of kingdoms, when Chaos’ initial assaults began on the Shattered Worlds, the spellsingers refused to leave their homeworld; preferring instead to stay behind and protect it from outside threats alongside other local heroes.

After the Collective succeeded in stabilizing the rifts that threatened so many planes and realities, a handful of curious spellsingers took their first steps beyond what they knew and into the wider universe. Since then, they have began training others in their unique brand of magic, the spellsong. They have found acceptance on several worlds, including Pnumadesi and Theia.

Role: A spellsinger’s spells are generally more supportive in nature, but there are those who focus on the rarer, sound-based damaging spells they share with bards and similar spellcasters. Combined with their spellsongs, they can be a formidible threat both as performers and combatants.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d6.

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.)

Class Skills

The spellsinger’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the spellsinger.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Spellsingers are proficient with all simple weapons. They are also proficient with light armor, but not with any shields. A spellsinger can cast spellsinger spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, a spellsinger wearing medium or heavy armor, or using a shield, incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multiclass spellsinger still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.

Spellcasting

A spellsinger casts arcane spells drawn from the spellsinger spell list (page xx). He can cast any spell he knows without preparing it ahead of time. Every spellsinger spell has a verbal component (usually rhythmic chanting or singing). To learn or cast a spell, a spellsinger must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level.

The Difficulty Class (DC) for a saving throw against a spellsinger’s spell is: 10 + the spell level + the spellsinger’s Charisma modifier

Like other spellcasters, a spellsinger can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. His base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Spellsinger. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if he has a high Charisma score.

The spellsinger’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A spellsinger begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the spellsinger’s choice. At each new spellsinger level, he gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Spellsinger Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a spellsinger knows is not affected by his Charisma score).

Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even spellsinger level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), a spellsinger can choose to learn a new spell in place of one he already knows. In effect, the spellsinger “loses” the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least one level lower than the highest-level spellsinger spell the spellsinger can cast. A spellsinger may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that he gains new spells known for the level.

A spellsinger need not prepare his spells in advance. He can cast any spell he knows at any time, assuming he has not yet used up his allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Cantrips: Spellsingers learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, as noted on Table: Spellsinger Spells Known under “Spells Known.” These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again.

Arcane Muse (Ex)

At 1st level, a spellsinger forms a powerful bond with a muse; a magical spirit drawn to the spellsinger’s potential that takes the form of a familiar. This functions as the familiar granted by the wizard’s arcane bond class feature, except as noted here.

It gains speak with master at 1st level. It does not grant the spellsinger Alertness as a bonus feat.
Its base Intelligence and Charisma are the same as the spellsinger’s, unless the spellsinger’s level would grant it a higher score.
At 5th level, it learns one of the spellsinger’s languages and can communicate normally with any creature with which it shares a language.
At 13th level instead of scry on familiar, it grants the spellsinger the ability to prepare one additional spellsong each day. This spellsong’s level must be at least 2 lower than the highest-level spell the spellsinger can cast.
Spellsongs (Sp)

Each morning, a spellsinger can spend 1 hour preparing spellsongs after he rests for at least 8 hours. When a spellsinger prepares spellsongs, he chooses one cantrip and one spell he knows of each indicated level (see Table: Spellsinger). The spellsinger can cast each of his prepared spells one additional time per day, and when he does, they gain the benefits of both the Eschew Materials and Still Spell feats without increasing their spell level or casting time. The spellsinger must still provide the verbal components required by all of his spellsinger spells (in addition to any focus or expensive material components).

Variant Spellsongs: Spellsongs can take a number of different forms beyond preparing spells to cast as described above, and a collection of those variations can be found at the end of this section.

Carry Tune (Su)

At 19th level, once per day, when an ally the spellsinger can hear casts a spell with a verbal component, the spellsinger can cast that same spell within 1 minute using one of his own spell slots of the same level. If the spell requires other components, the spellsinger must still provide them, and the spell requires a full-round action to cast (he can still apply metamagic feats to it).

If he casts that spell as a full-round action (or if it’s a quickened spell), it benefits from his spellsong class feature as if he prepared it. This otherwise functions as casting a spontaneous spell with a metamagic feat.

Spellsong Mastery (Ex)

At 20th level, a spellsinger no longer needs to rest for 8 hours to prepare spellsongs. Instead, he can spend 5 minutes to prepare a different spellsong in a slot he hasn’t spent for the day.

Variant Spellsongs

Unless stated otherwise, you can prepare any of these variant spellsongs once per day. Their benefits supercede the standard benefits of casting a spellsong.

Arcane Discovery

You gain an arcane discovery for which you meet any requirements using this slot’s level as your effective wizard level.

The effects of that discovery treat your effective wizard level as twice this slot’s level.

Arcane Exploit

You gain an arcane reservoir equal to half this slot’s level and one arcanist exploit from the following list. Arcane barrier, arcane weapon, aspect of innocence, charmer, consume magic items, counterspell, dimensional slide, invoke primal magic, metamixing, obfuscated spellcasting, orderly casting, philanthropic magic, primal magic, potent magic, redirect primal magic, resist primal magic, see magic, sonic blast, spell disruption, spell tinkerer, swift consume, wild stride

Cantrip Rhythm

You temporarily learn additional spellsinger cantrips equal to this slot’s level (minimum 1). This does not allow you to add those cantrips to a spellbook if you have one. You can prepare this variant spellsong in place of your cantrip when preparing spellsongs each day.

Empower Muse

Your muse also gains the added Hit Dice, base attack bonus, saves, feats, and Str/Dex bonus of an animal companion. Your effective druid level when determining these values is equal to twice this slot’s level.

Guarded Spellsong

You don’t provoke attacks of opportunity when you cast the spell prepared in this slot either as a prepared spell or a spontaneous spell.

Riff on Your Spells

You can prepare a willing ally’s spell as a spellsong in this slot, but that spell must be at least 1 level lower if it’s not on the spellsinger spell list. Allies must spend at least 1 minute with you discussing the chosen spells while you prepare them.

Songblade

You gain a morale bonus to all attacks equal to this slot’s level.

If you also have Songstrike, you can select this a second time to still gain the morale bonus, but only equal to half this slot’s level.

Songstrike

You must have Songblade prepared as a 3rd-level or higher spellsong to select this variant spellsong, and you must prepare this in the same or a higher-level slot (using Twin Spellsong).

Instead of granting you a morale bonus, Songblade increases your base attack bonus, which can grant you additional attacks as part of a full-attack action (You get a third attack when your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, and a fourth when it is +16 or higher, as the fighter).

Spellsong Book

You must have Spellsong Research prepared as a spellsong to select this variant spellsong. You can prepare spellsongs of this slot’s level or lower from an alchemist’s formula book or a prepared spellcaster’s spellbook, but only if those spells are on the spellsinger spell list.

The first time you prepare this variant spellsong, you can also generate your own spellbook as if you were a wizard of twice this slot’s level (minimum 1st), using your own spells known or spells made available to you by fellow alchemists, prepared spellcasters with spellbooks, or scrolls. This otherwise functions as copying spells into a spellbook, and may take longer than the usual 1 hour to complete. Any time you prepare this variant spellsong at a higher level, you can add the appropriate number of spells to your spellbook in the same way.

Spellsong Expertise

If the spellsong you prepare in this slot is at least 1 level lower, you can spend 5 minutes to prepare a different spellsong in this slot. If you have spellsong mastery, you can spend 1 minute instead.

Spellsong Research

You temporarily learn an additional spellsinger spell of this slot’s level that you can only prepare and cast as a spellsong. This spell can’t be added to a spellbook if you have one.

Spellsong Reservoir

You must have Arcane Exploit to select this variant spellsong.

Each day, when preparing spellsongs, your arcane reservoir fills with raw magical energy, gaining a number of points equal to 3 + this slot’s level. Any points you had from the previous day are lost, as are any points gained in excess of 3 + your spellsinger level.

You can expend 1 point from your arcane reservoir as a free action whenever you cast any spellsinger spell. If you do, you can choose to increase the caster level by 1 or increase the spell’s DC by 1. You can expend no more than 1 point from your reservoir on a given spell in this way.

Spontaneous Spellsongs

Spellsinger spells you cast that are exactly 3 levels below this slot’s level gain the benefits of spellsong.

Stuck in My Head

If the spellsong you prepare in this slot is at least 2 levels lower, you can concentrate on that spellsong as a swift action.

Twin Spellsong

You can divide this slot’s level between two spellsongs, preparing and using each individually.
